Asks.description:
What happens to the answer of an ask: where an agent's ask can run a command, and how an
outside ask's answer reaches the session that asked.

deliver.description:
The command that delivers an answer to the session that asked, relative to the factory
folder. It gets the ask's id, revision, session, `answered` or `dismissed`, and the answer
as its arguments. Without it, the answer is only stored.

targets.description:
The folders, besides the task's worktree, where an answer can run an ask's command, by
name. A relative folder is under the factory folder.

BatchDefaults.description: What `priory batch add` starts: the planning workflow, and the workflow each entry's task runs.

entries.description: The workflow of each entry's task; the `[request]` workflow when unset.

workflow.description: The workflow of a batch's planning task. It needs a human step after a model step: the go.

Caps.description:
The factory's spend caps, in dollars, which the daemon enforces from `prices.toml` and the
steps' token counts.

day.description: What the factory may spend in a local day.

lanes.description: Each lane's caps, by its `<team>/<theme>` name. A lane's day or week cap holds new starts.

week.description: What the factory may spend in a week from Monday 00:00 local time.

Cloud.description: `[cloud]`: the bounds of cloud runs, which take no room and whose cost Priory cannot read.

max.description: How many cloud runs a runner has at once, 4 when unset. Past it, a task waits to start one.

CloudwatchWebhook.description: CloudWatch alarm state changes, from an EventBridge API destination at `POST /hooks/cloudwatch`.

secret_env.description:
The environment variable that holds the API key value of the EventBridge connection, never
the value itself.

CommandGuard.description: A shell command that is irreversible: its program, then the first words after its options.

flags.description: When set, the command matches only with one of these options, such as `--prod`.

name.description: The guard's name, which a workflow's `guard.allow` names.

run.description: The program and the words it starts with, such as `["fly", "deploy"]`.

Consult.description: `[consult]`: the bounds of one consult, and `[consult.allow]`, who may consult whom.

allow.description:
Each asking agent's investigators, by the asking agent's name. An agent with no line
consults nobody.

cap.description: What one consult may cost, in dollars; 0.50 when unset.

deadline.description: How long from the `consult` call to its report, the wait for room included; 15m when unset.

per_task.description: How many consults one task may make; 5 when unset.

Decision.description:
A decision model: a command that answers typed questions with probabilities, and how much of
its answer Priory trusts.

agreement.description: The least share of labeled cases it must sort as the person did; 0.9 when unset.

daily_calls.description: The most calls the daemon makes in a day; 200 when unset.

evaluation.description: The file of a person's labeled cases, relative to the factory's folder, named `*.eval.toml`.

key_env.description:
The environment variable that holds the model's key, never the key itself. The command
sees it, `PATH` and `HOME`, and no other variable.

run.description:
The command, run with `sh -c` in the factory's folder. It reads the question as JSON on
stdin and prints the answer as JSON.

threshold.description: The least probability of an answer that Priory acts on; 0.9 when unset.

timeout.description: How long one call may run; 5s when unset, 30s at most.

Decisions.description:
`[decisions]`: the decision model of each decision point. A point with none keeps its own
behaviour.

triage.description: Sorts a person's feedback on a pull request before it wakes the task.

EventLog.description:
Where the event log lives: herdr-bus's file on this machine, or a Postgres database that
several machines share.

timeout.description:
How long one Postgres call may wait on the database before the log counts as unreachable;
10 seconds when unset.

url_env.description:
The environment variable that holds the Postgres connection string, `PRIORY_LOG_URL`
unless named: the file never holds the string itself.

Fair.description: What the queue takes turns between inside a band.

secret_env.description:
The environment variable that holds the passcode the webhook was created with, never the
passcode itself.
The environment variable that holds the webhook's secret, never the secret itself.

Guards.description: `[guard]` in `factory.toml`: the irreversible calls the factory adds to the built-in ones.

commands.description: Shell commands, each a guard of its own name.

tools.description: MCP tools by full name, such as `mcp__stripe__create_refund`, or a prefix ending in `*`.

secret_env.description:
The environment variable that holds the webhook recipient's Shared Secret, never the secret
itself.

IntakeSettings.description: `[intake]`: how the intake treats a failing poll.

alarm_after.description:
How long a source's polls fail before the intake posts its report, which the desk ranks as
an alarm; 15 minutes when unset. Until then the desk shows only its banner.

secret_env.description: The environment variable that holds the app's client secret, never the secret itself.

workspace.description:
The workspace id, such as `a86dr8yl`, whose notifications Priory takes. Intercom sends an
app's notifications from every workspace that installed it.

Kit.description:
A kit repository whose skills, instructions and memories every run gets, before the factory's
own. Each runner fetches it with git's own credentials.

every.description: How often a runner fetches the ref again; every 5 minutes when unset.

instructions.description: The instructions file inside the repository; `instructions.md` when unset.

memories.description: The memories folder inside the repository; `memories` when unset.

ref.description: The branch, tag or commit to fetch; the repository's default branch when unset.

repo.description:
The repository, as `git fetch` takes it: a URL, or a path, which a relative one takes from
the factory folder.

skills.description: The skills folder inside the repository; `skills` when unset.

Limits.description: Spend caps in dollars: per task, per local day and per week.

day.description: What may be spent in a local day.

week.description: What may be spent in a week from Monday 00:00 local time.

secret_env.description: The environment variable that holds the webhook's signing secret, never the secret itself.

McpServer.description: `[mcp.<name>]`: a person's statement about one MCP server of their own harness config.

read_only.description:
Where the service enforces that the server only reads, such as "The token has the
org:read and event:read scopes only." Priory cannot check it.

MemoriesRepo.description:
A memories repository whose memories every run gets, after the kit's and before the factory's
own, and where the daily pull request of accepted memories goes in place of the kit. Each runner
fetches it with git's own credentials.

every.description: How often a runner fetches the ref again; every 5 minutes when unset.

path.description: The memories folder inside the repository; `memories` when unset.

ref.description: The branch, tag or commit to fetch; the repository's default branch when unset.

repo.description:
The repository, as `git fetch` takes it: a URL, or a path, which a relative one takes from
the factory folder.

Notify.description: Where the daemon tells a person that the desk's next item changed, besides Web Push.

desktop.description:
Whether the daemon runs `notify-send` with the title of each new next item that is an ask
or an alarm.

age.description:
How long a task waits in the queue for each band it moves up in start order, up to the
highest band not in `preempt`; no task moves when unset.

fair.description: `lane` makes the queue take turns between lanes inside a band; oldest first when unset.

overlap.description: Whether a task waits for an earlier active task that changes the same files; true when unset.

preempt.description:
The bands whose waiting head may stop a run of a lower band at the end of its turn; none
when unset.

review_limit.description:
How many pull requests of a lane, or of a batch, may wait for a person before its new tasks
wait to start; no limit when unset. A task of the first band never waits.

Recipe.description:
One command of a repository's recipe: `argv`, which Priory execs as it is, or `shell`, which it
runs with `sh -c`.

argv.description: The program and its arguments, run with no shell.

timeout.description:
How long it may run before Priory kills it with its process group; `command_timeout` when
unset.

Repo.description:
`[repos."owner/name"]`: what the daemon runs in a worktree of the repository, so no run has to
find out how to install and build it.

cloud_setup.description:
A script in the repository that installs what its checks need in a Claude cloud session.
`priory cloud setup-script` copies it into the cloud environment's setup script. It holds
no secret: anyone who uses the environment can read it.

resume.description:
Runs after the daemon adds back the worktree a retirement removed, before its agent
starts. A failure blocks the task.

setup.description:
Runs after the daemon adds a task's new worktree, before its agent starts. A failure blocks
the task.

teardown.description: Runs before the sweep or a retirement removes the worktree. A failure keeps the worktree.

RequestDefaults.description: What `priory add` and `POST /api/request` use when a request names no workflow or band.

band.description: The band of a request that names none.

workflow.description: The workflow a request starts when it names none.

Resource.description: A resource the room check measures.

Runs.description: What happens when a run starts.

attach.description:
The command that opens a run where a person can watch it, relative to the factory folder.
The daemon runs it once per new run of a step with `attach = true`, with the task id and
run id as its arguments.

Sandbox.description:
`[sandboxes.<name>]`: a jail around a run's agent, which sees its worktree, its harness's own
home and what the sandbox names, each at the same path as outside.

env.description: The daemon's variables the run keeps, by name, beside the few every jailed run keeps.

read.description: Paths bound read-only, each absolute or under `~/`.

write.description: Paths bound read-write, each absolute or under `~/`.

oneOf.description: A bubblewrap jail: Linux only, with the `bwrap` program on `PATH`.

every.description:
How often the script runs, at least 10s, counted from its last run, a stall's run included;
only when `when` stalls the queue when unset.

run.description: A shell command, run by `sh -c` in `PRIORY_HOME`.

timeout.description: How long it may run before Priory kills it; 5 minutes when unset.

when.description: The resource whose shortage runs the script; it runs only on its `every` when unset.

Search.description: How tasks are found: who writes their TL;DR, and whether search compares embeddings too.

command.description: A command that reads text on stdin and prints a JSON array of floats, instead of `model`.

embeddings.description: Whether search compares embeddings of TL;DRs as well as keywords.

model.description: The embedding model Priory runs in process, a Hugging Face repository.

tldr.description: The agent whose model writes a new task's TL;DR; no summarizer runs without one.

secret_env.description: The environment variable that holds the integration's Client Secret, never the secret itself.

Serve.description: The HTTP server over the factory's state, in the daemon and in `priory serve`.

extension_origins.description:
The browser extensions whose pages may write, by exact origin, such as
`chrome-extension://<id>`. They still send the token.

listen.description: The address and port to listen on; a loopback address unless `public` is set.

public.description: Whether `listen` may be an address beyond this machine.

redact_env.description: More environment variables whose values the terminal hides, besides the factory's secrets.

terminal.description:
Whether a token holder may watch a run's terminal, its screen with known secrets hidden, and
type into it.

token_env.description: The environment variable that holds the token clients send, never the token itself.

url.description:
The address a person opens the server at, such as `https://runner.example.ts.net:7390`,
which links in a pull request body start with.

web.description: Whether to serve the web view's files as well as `/api`.

SlackShortcut.description: The "Queue in Priory" message shortcut, which the intake receives over Slack's Socket Mode.

token_env.description: The environment variable that holds the app-level token (`xapp-`), never the token itself.

users.description:
The Slack user ids, such as `U0123ABCD`, allowed to queue a task; the shortcut refuses
everyone else.

Sweep.description:
How the daemon frees room: the built-in worktree sweep, the person's scripts, and the sweeper
agent it starts when they do not free enough.

after.description:
How long the queue stays stalled after its scripts ran before the sweeper starts; 30 minutes
when unset.

agent.description: The agent of the built-in `sweep` workflow; no sweeper starts without one.

every.description: How often the built-in worktree sweep runs; every 10 minutes when unset.

repo.description: The repository the sweeper works in and files its issue on, a GitHub `owner/name`.

scripts.description: Scripts run when the resource they name stalls the queue.

Telemetry.description: Where the daemon exports its trace records as OpenTelemetry spans.

headers_env.description:
The environment variable that holds the headers each request carries, such as an API key,
as `key1=value1,key2=value2` with URL-encoded values. Never the headers themselves.

metrics.description: The metric groups each process sends to the endpoint's `/v1/metrics`; none sends no metric.

metrics_cap.description: The data points a process sends per minute at most, over a rolling minute; 1000 when unset.

metrics_every.description: How often a process samples its groups and sends one request, at least 10s; 60s when unset.

otlp.description: The OTLP/HTTP base URL, such as `http://127.0.0.1:4318`; spans go to its `/v1/traces`.

Terminal.description: What the HTTP server lets a token holder do with a run's terminal.

oneOf.description: Watch, and let a person take a run's keyboard and type into its pane.

Webhooks.description: The signed webhooks the HTTP server accepts, by source.

description: `factory.toml` or `factory.yaml`: the factory's name and the daemon's settings.

bands.description: The bands, highest first, when they are not the default ones.

caps.description: Spend caps in dollars for every task, and for each lane by its name.

command_timeout.description: How long one git, gh or tmux command may run before Priory kills it.

consult.description: Who may consult which investigator, and the bounds of one consult.

critic.description:
The scorer that grades a plan no person reads: a grade that leads to a model or code step
of a task without `intervention = "plan"`. It can only refuse the grade.

decisions.description: A decision model for each decision point that names one.

gate.description: The project's gate: the command `priory gate` runs with `sh -c` in a task's worktree.

guard.description: Irreversible commands and MCP tools on top of the built-in ones.

handler.description: The agent whose model reads a stalled run's screen; no handler runs without one.

links.description:
Autolinks, in order: each key a regex, each value an `https://` URL template whose `$1`
names the regex's first group. An entry with a built-in link's regex replaces it.

mcp.description: What a person states about each MCP server an investigator names, by the server's name.

pre_review.description:
The judge that reads a step's lessons before an approval step asks a person: a result that
repeats one goes back to the agent once. It can only send the result back.

repos.description:
Recipes by repository, each key a GitHub `owner/name`: the commands the daemon runs in a
task's worktree of that repository.

sandboxes.description: Each sandbox a workflow can turn on with `sandbox`, by its name.

stalled.description: How long a run goes without a hook event or a change on its pane before it counts as stalled.

trust_worktrees.description:
Priory records Claude Code's and Codex's folder trust for the worktrees and clones it
creates for the repositories the factory names, so no run stops on a trust dialog.

writing.description:
A writing guide, as a path relative to the factory folder. Priory appends its text to the
system prompt of every agent it starts.

title: factory.toml
